# Change Management for a Mandatory Global AI Rollout
## "One Standard, Many Adoption Paths"

---

## 1. The core diagnostic

Mandatory AI rollouts in regulated multinationals fail in six recognisable ways, and all six are versions of the same mistake: treating AI adoption as a **tool deployment** when it is in fact a **simultaneous renegotiation of the employment bargain, the professional-liability regime, and the data-processing posture across every jurisdiction, works council and regulated decision process you operate in.**

**A licence is not an adoption. A seat is not a jurisdiction.** Your unit of exposure is *this work type, performed by this employee, in this legal entity, under this works agreement, feeding this regulated decision.* A claims adjuster summarising a file that becomes a denial letter and a marketing manager drafting an internal deck are not the same activity, are not governed by the same rules, and must not appear on the same dashboard as the same number.

**You have put a proxy on a performance dashboard, so you now measure the proxy.** Usage-per-head is the cheapest metric in the system to fake and the most expensive to interpret. Within two quarters you have prompt-padding, tool-theatre, scheduled keystroke rituals, and managers coaching teams on how to look adopted. Worse: **your dashboard currently rewards dishonesty and punishes candour.** The teams reporting low usage while using it covertly score badly. The teams performing compliance-under-hierarchy — high usage, zero value — score well. The number is not merely noisy; its sign is wrong.

**Covert use is your most valuable signal, and you have criminalised it.** A team hiding its AI use has already proven the value proposition to itself, at personal risk, without central support. It is hiding for one of four reasons: fear of headcount attribution, a local prohibition it disagrees with, professional-liability exposure, or distrust of what HQ does with the data. Every one of those is fixable. Meanwhile covert use *is* shadow AI: client PII in consumer chatbots, no logging, no retention control, no AI Act traceability, no defensibility if a regulator asks how a claim decision was reached. **The mandate is making your single largest actual risk worse, because the sanctioned channel now carries a surveillance cost the unsanctioned one does not.**

**"Cultural resistance" is an explanatory dead end, and usually a mislabelling of institutional rights.** German co-determination over performance-monitoring technology (BetrVG §87(1)(6)) is not a temperament. A French CSE consultation, a Dutch works council right of consent, a Nordic collective agreement, an Italian Art. 4 Statuto dei Lavoratori restriction on remote monitoring — these are binding legal gates that someone skipped. What is being reported to the steering committee as "the Germans are resistant" is, in fact, "we deployed an individual-monitoring system without the consultation the law requires, and legal counsel there noticed." Conversely, high-adoption markets may simply be high-power-distance environments where instruction compliance is fast and honest feedback is slow. **The adoption curve is measuring six different things in six places and cannot be compared.**

**Professional-pride resistance is disproportionately your best people, and is usually a correct quality signal.** Senior underwriters, qualified actuaries, complex-loss adjusters and reserving specialists objecting that "this tool is confidently wrong about treaty wording / about the difference between a policy exclusion and a condition precedent" are giving you free model evaluation. They also carry personal professional obligations (IFoA/SOA actuarial standards, local broker and adjuster licensing, Lloyd's market conduct rules) that no HQ mandate overrides. Classifying them as laggards on a Rogers curve is how you lose the people who own your loss ratio.

**Headcount fear cannot be answered with reassurance — only with an instrument.** If the honest answer is "yes, some roles shrink, mostly through attrition and redeployment," then saying "no one will lose their job because of AI" is a one-time trust expenditure with permanent consequences. The moment the first restructuring lands, every future change programme in the group is contaminated. Vague comfort is more damaging than an honest, bounded, written commitment.

**Ratchet: anything on a performance dashboard becomes an employment-law artifact.** Individual AI-usage scores are discoverable in unfair-dismissal, discrimination and works-council proceedings; they may constitute automated processing requiring a DPIA and, in some jurisdictions, prior consultation or consent. Under the EU AI Act, employment-context systems used for evaluating workers sit in the high-risk category. You have built a retrofit you will pay for twice — once to build, once to unwind under legal deadline.

---

## 2. The resolution

**Separate the risk mandate from the productivity ambition. They have been fused, and that fusion is the whole problem.**

- The **risk mandate** is: *if you use AI for company work, you use the approved channel.* This is legitimately mandatory, globally, non-negotiable, and it is the actual reason a mandate exists.
- The **productivity ambition** is: *the work gets done faster and better.* This is measured at team-outcome level, is never mandatory per keystroke, and is achieved by making the sanctioned tool the **easiest and safest** option rather than the compulsory one.

**The one-sentence answer: outcomes are global; adoption paths are local. Mandate the channel and the capability, never the keystroke.**

An underwriter in Munich and one in Singapore are held to the same turnaround time, the same quality gate, the same data boundary and the same accountability rule. They differ only in *how, when and under what local agreement they got there.*

---

## 3. What is actually mandatory (restated)

| Old mandate | New mandate |
|---|---|
| Every knowledge worker must use the toolkit | Every knowledge worker must be **licensed, trained and AI-literate** (already a legal obligation under EU AI Act Art. 4 — use it as the frame) |
| Usage metrics feed performance dashboards | **Channel compliance** is a conduct rule; **team outcomes** are a performance measure; **individual usage is neither** |
| Regional exceptions granted ad hoc | **Consultation gate** must pass before go-live; exceptions are named, owned, dated and expiring |
| — | If you use AI for company work, it is the **approved channel or nothing** — enforced technically, not by dashboard |

This preserves 100% of the governance value of the mandate and discards the coercion that generates gaming. It is also the version you can defend to a works council, a data-protection authority and EIOPA in the same meeting.

---

## 4. Six-layer architecture, with a divergence cap

| Layer | Contents | Variation policy |
|---|---|---|
| **L0 — Global invariants** | Data boundary (no customer PII, claims files, medical data or underwriting submissions to non-approved endpoints); named accountable human for every customer-affecting output; **no adverse customer decision (declinature, pricing loading, claim denial, fraud referral) may rest on model output without documented human adjudication**; full prompt/output logging for Tier 2–3 work; model inventory and AI Act risk classification; **no individual-level covert monitoring, ever**; existing professional sign-off requirements unchanged | **Zero variation.** Applies in every entity including carve-outs. |
| **L1 — Global platform** | One toolkit, one identity/SSO, one logging plane, one evaluation harness, one use-case catalogue, one shared prompt/pattern library, one incident channel | Zero variation in *what*; variation permitted in *hosting region* only. |
| **L2 — Work-type governance tiers** | Governs by **the work, not the country** (see below) | Zero variation. The tier definitions are global. |
| **L3 — Legal & consultation gate** | Works council / CSE / OR agreements, union bargaining, DPIAs, data residency, local regulator notification (e.g. NYDFS, BaFin, FCA, MAS, IRDAI), local employment-law review of any telemetry | **High variation, time-boxed.** No country goes live before its gate closes. No country may sit behind the gate >2 quarters without an executive owner and a written recovery plan. |
| **L4 — Adoption path & pace** | Sequence of use cases, coaching model, language coverage and model-quality remediation, champion structures, sponsorship level, training format, incentive framing | **Free variation within budget.** Local leadership owns this outright. |
| **L5 — Measurement & incentives** | What appears on which dashboard, at what aggregation, seen by whom | Global schema; **local suppression rights** where telemetry is restricted. |

**Divergence cap.** Permanent divergence is limited to jurisdictions where L1 is legally impossible — realistically China (separate approved-model list, cross-border data transfer regime, separate release train, separate publisher-of-record equivalent) and any sanctioned or hard-blocked entity. Everything else is temporary by construction: every exception carries a named executive owner, a stated reason drawn from a closed list (legal gate / language quality / regulated-decision validation pending / active dispute), an expiry date, and quarterly review at group level. **Exceptions with no expiry date are not granted.**

---

## 5. Work-type tiers (governs by the work, not the passport)

| Tier | Examples | Rule | Metric |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T0 — Personal / internal, no customer data** | Meeting notes, internal drafting, translation of internal docs, code scaffolding, learning | **Unrestricted, unlogged at individual level, unmeasured.** Actively encouraged. | None. Deliberately none. |
| **T1 — Internal analysis on internal data** | Portfolio synthesis, competitor scans, MI narrative, policy-wording comparison for internal use | Approved channel, logged, sampled QA | Team-level quality sample |
| **T2 — Customer- or intermediary-facing output** | Broker correspondence, claims comms, quote documentation, complaint responses | Named human sign-off; four-eyes for first 90 days per user; retained audit trail | Error rate, complaint rate, rework |
| **T3 — Regulated decision input** | Underwriting risk assessment, pricing/rating, reserving, claims adjudication, fraud referral, suitability | **Model risk management regime applies.** Validation, documented performance, bias testing, challenger review, actuarial/underwriting authority unchanged. General-purpose LLM use prohibited without validated wrapper and sign-off. AI Act high-risk obligations presumed. | Overturn rate on appeal, disparate-impact testing, model-validation status |

This tiering does the single most useful thing available: it lets you be **maximally permissive at T0** (where nearly all the "productivity" actually lives and where nearly all the covert use is happening) while being **maximally conservative at T3** — instead of splitting the difference everywhere and satisfying no one.

---
